newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks turn around, end up on Telmex hopes.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks turn around, end up on Telmex hopes.

text.p: Mexican stocks rebounded at support and closed up on Wednesday after being hauled by heavyweight Telmex, on favorable expectations for earnings which it is due to report on Thursday, traders said.

"The IPC has a very important support at 3,220 points. When it rebounded there, buyers stepped in and Telmex in particular was in heavy demand," said Jaime Fernandez, technical analyst at the Interacciones brokerage.
The blue chip IPC index closed up 16.70 points, or 0.51 percent, at 3,264.54. Volume was much improved at 97.7 million shares traded.

Telmex has the heaviest weighting of stocks included in the IPC, and its series L shares closed up 24 centavos at 12.28 pesos. Telmex ADRs closed up 5/8 at 31-3/8 in New York, despite the Dow Jones closing down 0.42 percent at 6,036.46 points.
Some traders said that local and foreign bottom-fishing buyers were also responsible for the recovery.
"Buyers were on the sidelines but prepared to step in at certain price levels. Some stocks had been hit too hard, and then they stepped in," said a trader at the Arka brokerage.
"Also, some went short this morning over the panic with the peso, and had to buy at the close," he added.

The peso was hit by a frenzy of speculation in early trade, which many dealers put down to comments by U.S. economist Rudiger Dornbusch, a leading critic of official Mexican policy towards the peso. Dornbusch was quoted by the local paper, Reforma, as saying the peso should devalue by 20 percent, to about nine per dollar.
Speculation let up when Dornbusch was reported as saying later in the day by Banco Santander in New York that a year-end rate of eight pesos per dollar would be adequate.
The 48-hour peso recovered a little, but still closed six pesos weaker at 7.85/7.85 per dollar.
On the broad market, losers outnumbered gainers by 44 to 35, out of 99 stocks that changed hands.
Gainers included video distributors Grupo Videovisa, which reported earnings during the session, and beverage firms Ggemex and Valle, which reported on Tuesday.

Percentage losers were headed by financial stocks GFMulti and GFinver. Traders said that financial stocks often slid in the wake of primary rate hikes, such as those seen on Tuesday night, when Banco de Mexico assigned benchmark 28-day Cetes at 27.70 percent, or 180 basis points above last week.
